findings.message: Round-4 B1 finding: this is an instance fix. Starting hand-made numbers at 1001 only protects projects that already have a specclaw row. Three cases still collide and lose a spec change on every sync. (1) Proposals made by hand before the first sync. The new LG test writes this in as expected: `skipped: ["LG-001…"]`. (2) Hand-made proposals created under the old numbering in projects that are already synced, such as an existing RB-002. Nothing renumbers them. (3) Spec changes numbered 1000 or higher, which share the hand-made range (change 1001 and hand-made RB-1001). The finding asked that all spec records sync. Fix: give the two kinds keys that can't collide, for example a separate prefix for hand-made keys. Alternatively, migrate or reassign hand-made keys that sit on spec numbers when a project is first synced. Add a test where a pre-existing hand-made LG-001 and spec 001 both end up present.
findings.scenario: Project LG has a hand-made LG-001, then gets synced with change 001-a. Every sync reports `LG-001 skipped`, and change 001 never appears in delivery.

findings.message: The fix tells a retried confirm what happened the first time, but the cancel path does not. cancelAction swallows every NotPendingError, including `decision: "confirmed"`. cancelChat then returns normally and Chat.tsx shows 'Cancelled. Nothing was changed.' even though the write ran. An unknown action id is also reported as a successful cancel. Fix: when the decision is not 'cancelled', rethrow from cancelAction, or return the decision. Show 'already done' for 'confirmed' and an error for null, and test both cases.
findings.scenario: Add it → the write succeeds but the reply is lost → the user clicks Cancel → the UI says 'Cancelled. Nothing was changed.' while proposal CON-018 exists.

findings.message: claim() records `decided = confirmed` before registry.call runs, and removes it only if the call fails. While the write is still running, a second confirm reads 'confirmed' and gets 'This was already done.' If the write then fails, the card goes back to pending and nothing was done. An in-flight write is reported as done. Fix: record 'confirmed' only after the call succeeds, and treat a claim in progress as its own state ('in progress', not 'done').
findings.scenario: Double-click Add it while the tool call is slow and then throws ForbiddenError → the second click shows 'This was already done.', but nothing was written.

findings.message: Round-4 B3 finding asked that unknown ids stay an error. confirmChat now returns a plain error for them, but the UI still puts every non-ok result that isn't 'confirmed' into the 'cancelled' state. That covers an unknown action id, 'conversation not found', and a tool failure where the engine puts the card back in pending. Each one is drawn as a closed, cancelled card with no buttons. Fix: show 'cancelled' only when `r.earlier === "cancelled"`. Show other errors as an error state and keep the retry buttons when the server restored the card.
findings.scenario: confirmChat(convo, 'not-an-action') → returns {ok:false, error:"that action isn't in this conversation"} → the card is shown as cancelled. Or registry.call throws → the server card is pending again, but the UI shows it as cancelled.

findings.message: The comment says every path that closes a project records closed_at. Two paths don't. The trigger fires only on `UPDATE OF status`, so a project inserted as closed (fixtures, imports) gets closed_at null. The migration also doesn't backfill projects that are already closed. In both cases the project retention entry (`start: { at: ["closed_at"] }`, no idle) never starts, and manager names are kept forever. Fix: make the trigger `before insert or update of status`, and backfill closed_at for existing closed rows (for example from updated_at). Test the insert path and an existing closed row.
findings.scenario: A project that is already status='closed' when 0006 runs, or one inserted with status='closed' → closed_at stays null → manager_name is never anonymised.

findings.message: `FAILURES[name] ?? FAILURES[code]` looks the key up on a plain object literal, so prototype keys match. An error whose code or name is 'toString' or 'constructor' returns a function, and its source text is put into the model message. Use `Object.hasOwn` or a Map.
findings.scenario: A tool throws {code:'toString'} → the model receives 'read_ticket function toString() { [native code] } (reference …)'.
